name: tof_3

pyzx teleport.note: the benchmark's `optimized`, proved equivalent in the repository

pyzx full_reduce.note: PyZX 0.9.0 full_reduce + extraction, from benchmarks/survey/results.json; numerically exact, no proof

tzap 0.6.1 -O2 --decompose-rz --decompos.note: the twin of the equivalence task tof_3_tzap; numerically exact (numpy, full unitary), no proof

known_leaks: the original is a promoted benchmark of this repository (CircuitEq/Benchmarks/Tof3.lean), whose PyZX twin (T-count 19) and its proof are in the repository and its history, so a model may have seen both; removed from the run copy: the module, README.md, benchmarks/, the window table of scripts/certificate.py, and the hand alignment in the self-test of scripts/tcount_survey.py

CircuitEqTest/PhasePoly.lean keeps three test theorems about sub-blocks of this circuit (`tof3_merge`, `tof3_controls`, `tof3_core`); the harness removes CircuitEqTest/ from every run copy (on a base from before that library existed they sit in CircuitEq/PhasePoly.lean, unredacted)
scripts/tcount_survey.py generates this original (`tof(3)`) and scripts/check_pyzx_benchmarks.py names the PyZX pipeline that was used on it; calling PyZX is allowed anyway

CircuitEq/Benchmarks/BarencoTof3.lean is held out as well: it is the same Toffoli decomposition through the same PyZX pipeline, with its optimised twin and the windows of its proof, which give this task's answer away
